pr_title: [WIP] FIX: MSVC compiler missing header breaking debugging
pr_body:
Fixes #40666 

Caused by a problem in the MSVC compiler, and thread_local on windows.
pr_comments: Can you try to get this upstreamed too? Or a better version of it without the capslocks :P
Don't merge only fixes win32... so not the entire fix.

> Is it related to [onqtam/doctest#381](https://github.com/onqtam/doctest/issues/381) ?

he missed platform fix see new commit
It seems like it's possible to get into editor in 50% of times with current changes (compared to 30%), but I still get crashes on startup while debugging. D:

> It seems like it's possible to get into editor in 50% of times with current changes (compared to 30%), but I still get crashes on startup while debugging. D:

OK I updated all to use thread_local statically with the windows platform only.

Please let me know if the crash is gone
No, it may have improved the situation, but I might have just got lucky enough to run it 10 times in a row, but then crashes again 5 times in a row. 😄
Closing: this fix 'kind of worked' but its mostly a hack, we can fix with swapping to /MD but ideally don't want to do this.

issue_context.title: Crash with doctest on attempting to debug the editor when compiling with `tests=yes`
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**

**OS/device including version:**

target=debug, bits=64

![2020-07-24](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17108460/88413038-27f72500-cde3-11ea-8ba3-601abe1b0f13.png)


Running the editor or tests without debugger works fine.

**Steps to reproduce:**
Compile the engine with `scons tests=yes`: #40696.

I'm using the [C++ extension for VSCode](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/languages/cpp) to debug Godot with Visual Studio Windows debugger, with the configuration file similar to this:

```json
{
    "version": "0.2.0",

            "type": "cppvsdbg",

            "program": "${workspaceFolder}/bin/godot.windows.tools.64.4.exe",

}

**Minimal reproduction project:**
Happens even on project manager startup.
comments: As discussed in IRC full rebuild fixes this issue

Reopening because it now happens sporadically. :eyes:

When I do manage to startup the editor, I get either #40667 or #40654 on exiting Godot while debugging. I then stop the debugging forcefully, and when try to debug again, I get *this* crash. Stopping the debugging again and now can launch the editor, and the same steps can be repeated.

That's with full engine rebuild as described above: `git clean -xdf`.
I will look into this now and see if this happens on OSX too, under the same conditions.
If not will try out MSVC/vscode on windows
Some good news OSX cannot reproduce this, so indeed it's isolated to VSCode on windows with MSVC.

```

I get this trace rarely, like need to start debug 10 times, but mostly I get the call stack as described in the issue above.

@RevoluPowered still getting crashes with #40681, but I got curious whether removing all `DOCTEST_THREAD_LOCAL` occurrences in `doctest.h` could help, and it does, I cannot reproduce this anymore... I'm also able to run tests without issues: `.\bin\godot.windows.tools.64.exe --test -s`

Same crash if compiled under VS2017 or VS2019 toolchains.

Found very similar issue regarding `thread_local` crashes:

https://github.com/tinycthread/tinycthread/issues/44

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thread-local_storage#Windows_implementation

BTW, have anyone tested Mingw build? `thread_local` seems to be part of C-runtime not C++, Mingw is probably using the same default Windows UCRT, and Godot is linking runtime statically to avoid dependency on `libstdc++`.
